**Question Explanation : Among the following how many compounds, on elimination give regioselective products
$ $**Concept: Elimination reaction
$ $**Solution: Regioselectivity is possible when an elimination reaction can produce two or more constitutionally isomeric products.
$ $(i) 2-bromobutane can eliminate HBr to form but-1-ene or but-2-ene.
$ $(ii) 2-bromo-2-methylpropane can only form 2-methylprop-1-ene.
$ $(iii) (1-bromoethyl)cyclohexane can form (vinyl)cyclohexane or ethylidenecyclohexane.
$ $(iv) 3-bromo-2,2-dimethylpentane can form 2,2-dimethylpent-1-ene or 2,2-dimethylpent-2-ene.
$ $(v) 3-bromo cyclohexan-1-one can form cyclohex-2-en-1-one or cyclohex-3-en-1-one.
$ $(vi) 4-bromo cyclohexan-1-one can only form cyclohex-3-en-1-one.
$ $(vii) 3-bromocyclohex-1-ene can form cyclohex-1,3-diene or cyclohex-1,4-diene.
$ $(viii) Cyclohexyl diazonium salt can only form cyclohexene.
$ $(ix) 1-phenylpropane-1,2-diol can eliminate water to form 1-phenylprop-1-en-2-ol or 2-phenylprop-1-en-1-ol (which tautomerizes).
$ $**Final Answer: 3
